# Filming

## Film

### Yap types: standard, walking, car
<a id="film-yap-formats"></a>

The simplest creator format, phone on a tripod: standard yap (sitting), walking yap (FaceTime-with-a-friend feel, not for beginners), car yap (candid). "The key to the yap is you just do it."

> The key to the yap is you just do it.

### Frame low, leave headroom for graphics
<a id="film-framed-graphic-headroom"></a>

Framed graphic yap: frame yourself low with space above your head for a graphic; plan head, caption and graphic placement and keep graphics vertical.

> Keep graphics vertical

### Tripod + Bluetooth remote + plug-in mic
<a id="film-yap-gear"></a>

iPhone on a ~$50 tripod with extending legs and a Bluetooth remote, plus a Røde USB-C plug-in mic or wired EarPods. AirPods do not work.

> AirPods do not work

### Pause in silence to think
<a id="film-recut-pause-method"></a>

Whenever you need to think, stop and stay silent with eye contact, then talk again; remove silences later (ReCut or silence removal). A 6–7 min raw clip is fine.

`film` · formats: reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches: all · stated · from [L06](../sources/L06.md)

Related: [Re-record the intro at the end](../topics/filming.md#film-redo-intro-at-end), [Axial jump cuts every 3–6 words](../topics/editing.md#edit-axial-jump-cuts)

### Re-record the intro at the end
<a id="film-redo-intro-at-end"></a>

The intro matters most but is where you're most awkward; after ~3 minutes you're in flow, so record the intro again then.

### iPhone 15: frame rates, modes, HDR
<a id="film-iphone15-frame-rates"></a>

4K 30 default; 4K 60 for reps you'll slow; 4K 24 for travel; 240 fps slo-mo for single moments; Action mode handheld; Cinematic mode for B-roll; HDR Video off for heavy grading (no Log/ProRes on the base 15).

`film` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all, gym, travel · our-take · from [SP](../sources/SP.md)

Related: [Specs: 9:16 reels, 4:5 or 3:4 feed](../topics/growth.md#growth-format-specs)

### Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight
<a id="film-iphone15-lens-choice"></a>

The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.

`film` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches: all, gym, travel · our-take · from [SP](../sources/SP.md)

Related: [Lock AE/AF, grid on, clean lens](../topics/filming.md#film-lock-ae-af)

### Lock AE/AF, grid on, clean lens
<a id="film-lock-ae-af"></a>

Long-press to lock exposure and focus, then drop exposure 0.3–0.7 to save highlights; Grid and Level on; clean the lens before every shoot; 48 MP photos for landscapes you'll crop.

`film` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches: all · our-take · from [SP](../sources/SP.md)

### Gym filming: etiquette and side light
<a id="film-gym-side-light"></a>

Never film others without consent, don't hog kit, keep the tripod out of walkways; avoid windows and mirrors and let overhead light hit the muscle from the side; film when quieter.

`film` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches: gym · our-take · from [SP](../sources/SP.md)

Related: [Two angles per exercise](../topics/filming.md#film-two-angles)

### Tripod height changes the story
<a id="film-tripod-heights"></a>

Low (41–60 cm) makes lifts look powerful; chest height is neutral; high (120–133 cm, tilted 10–20°) shows symmetry. A light tripod: thickest legs first, column down, legs spread, bag hung on it, out of plate paths.

`film` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: gym · our-take · from [SP](../sources/SP.md)

Related: [Gym angles: chest, shoulders, arms, abs](../topics/filming.md#film-angles-chest)

### Solo: record, then walk in
<a id="film-solo-start"></a>

Start recording and walk into frame (trim later), or use the 3 s/10 s timer; a watch or Bluetooth remote is faster.

## Mindset

### Quality is defined by the audience
<a id="film-quality-audience-defined"></a>

The audience decides what quality is, not the creator or the gear; some of the most viral videos are shot at night on a phone.

> Your audience is who determines what quality is, not you.
